paragraphs: Rotary cannon are the design fiction reaches for whenever a weapon needs to look serious. The spinning barrel cluster is instantly legible, and doubling it is the visual equivalent of shouting, which is exactly why it belongs on a vehicle that is not real.
The model is light at 28,744 polygons and 30,086 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to real time use. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits game weapons and vehicles, science fiction film and animation, concept art, previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A flight helmet is a headset with armour around it. Communications, hearing protection and a visor all have to be integrated rather than worn together, because there is no room under a headliner for anything that stacks.

The model is light at 27,010 polygons and 28,148 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps all at 4096x4096, in a generic scheme with no markings. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 it suits aviation and defence visualisation, equipment marketing, character accessories, training material, film props, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.
Twin tone horns work because two notes a fixed interval apart carry further and are harder to ignore than one. The trumpet shape is not styling either: the length of the flare is what sets the pitch.
The model is very light at 10,095 polygons and 10,012 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries StemCell certification.
At $49 it suits automotive parts visualisation, aftermarket and e-commerce imagery, technical illustration, engine bay scenes, game assets and editorial work. On sale since 2021.

Two glasses is a whole narrative. One bottle and one glass is a different scene entirely, and the props department knows it, which is why the pairing turns up in advertising for everything from hotels to jewellery.
The model holds 32,864 polygons and 33,133 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, supplying the bucket together with the glasses. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits hospitality and beverage visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, advertising, interior and event scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Most of an iceberg is not the part that gets photographed, and the visible shape is decided by how the whole mass balances underwater. They roll without warning when that balance changes, which is why nothing gets close to one on purpose.
The model is light at 19,567 polygons and 19,571 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so several can populate an ocean scene. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 it suits polar and marine visualisation, climate and documentary graphics, education material, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

The denim jacket has survived every fashion cycle since it was workwear, and the reason is the fit: short, boxy and cut to be worn over something. Buttoned up it reads as deliberate rather than casual, which changes the character wearing it.
The garment is light at 17,041 polygons and 17,296 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, buttoned up. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits apparel and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, character wardrobe work, advertising, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A flying wing loitering munition has no fuselage to speak of and no landing gear at all, because it is not expected to land. The delta shape is chosen for stability at low speed with almost nothing controlling it.

The model is extremely light at 4,873 polygons and 5,102 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and desert and winter camouflage builds are offered separately.
At $49 it suits defence visualisation, news and documentary graphics, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.
A palletising robot is a specialist. It moves boxes from a line to a pallet all day, so the arm is built for reach and speed in a horizontal plane rather than for the dexterity a welding robot needs.

The model holds 310,736 polygons and 319,558 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 18 maps, 2 at 4096x4096, 15 at 2048x2048 and one at 1024x1024. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $49 it suits manufacturing and logistics visualisation, robotics marketing, warehouse and factory scenes, training material and game environments. On sale since 2016.

The teach pendant is how a robot is actually programmed: somebody stands next to it, drives the arm to a position by hand and records it. The enabling switch on the back is a safety device that has to be held at exactly the right pressure.
The model is light at 25,614 polygons and 13,384 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $49 it suits robotics and automation visualisation, equipment marketing, interface mockups, training material, factory scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Wind turbines are far bigger than photographs suggest, and the blades turn far more slowly than people expect. Both facts follow from the same engineering: to catch more wind you make the rotor larger, and a larger rotor must turn slower or its tips go supersonic.
The model holds 100,035 polygons and 113,750 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits energy and infrastructure visualisation, renewable presentation, landscape and aerial scenes, documentary graphics, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Plaster monuments were produced in quantity from moulds, which is why so many identical heads exist and why so many survived in storage after the statues came down. As an object it is now historical evidence rather than sculpture.
The model is supplied as the head in white, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $49 it suits historical and documentary visualisation, museum and exhibition work, period film and television, education material, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A hydraulic splitter is slow on purpose. Wood splits along the grain when pushed steadily rather than struck, and the whole machine is built to apply several tonnes gradually instead of the impact an axe delivers.
The model is built at subdivision level, 73,410 polygons and 74,272 vertices with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $49 it suits tool and equipment marketing, workshop and outdoor visualisation, e-commerce imagery, training material, film props and game environments. On sale since 2021.

The street furniture contract is the deal that pays for the shelter: an advertising panel on the side funds the bench and the roof, which is why bus stops in most cities are designed by an advertising company rather than a transport one.
The model holds 89,139 polygons and 93,705 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, in black, and carries StemCell certification.

At $49 it suits urban and architectural visualisation, street furniture and advertising mockups, transport presentation, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

An implant is a screw in the jawbone with a tooth built on top of it, and the reason it works is that titanium bonds to bone rather than sitting against it. Showing one in section is how any patient is ever persuaded that this is a good idea.

The model is very light at 8,995 polygons and 9,125 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps all at 4096x4096, so it runs in interactive material. It carries StemCell certification.
At $49 it suits dental education and patient explanation, implant and clinic marketing, medical illustration, interactive learning and editorial work. On sale since 2019.
